description: Persona smoke expectations for 'mcdonalds' (Rick's PR #108 second review: moved out of shared C# -- tests/conformance/tests/Conformance.Tests/PersonaSmokeTests.cs -- so no brand-specific literal lives there; a data-only pack PR adds only this file). Loaded by PersonaSmokeExpectations.For(personaId). Every field must be sourced from this SAME persona's own pack files, never invented: greetingSubstring from personas/mcdonalds/prompts/greeting.yaml, and searchableOwnItem/orderableItemName/orderableItemSize/orderableItemPrice from personas/mcdonalds/menu/menuItems.json (the size/price pair must match that file's entry exactly, or the add-to-order smoke step fails). Brian's decision (#78): McDonald's has NO happy hour at all -- every one of this pack's 70 menu items carries happyHourDiscounted:false, so there is no per-item opt-in to avoid the way a happy-hour-enabled pack would need to; 'Hamburger' is simply the pack's cheapest, plainest item, chosen for readability. This generic smoke Theory does not itself assert happy-hour banner/clock behavior for real packs (that proof is fixture-pack-only, in PersonaHappyHourConformanceTests.cs), so McDonald's having no happy hour needs no extra field here. Refs #127 follow-up (Rick's scope comment on #127): mealNumber (query/number) is loaded by RealPackMealNumberConformanceTests.cs's PersonaMealNumberSmokeExpectations.For(personaId, isOptIn) -- required because this pack's own persona.json sets strategies.searchQueryRewrite:"meal_numbers". 'number' names a mealNumber value from this SAME pack's own menu/menuItems.json that resolves to MORE THAN ONE item (here, both the breakfast 'Egg McMuffin(R) Meal' and the lunch 'Big Mac(R) Meal' share mealNumber "1"), so the Theory's own overlap assertion is genuinely exercised; the expected item names themselves are never written here -- they are read fresh from menuItems.json by the Theory. #165 follow-up: this overlap is also the exact one #165's own menu-mode filtering is designed NOT to touch -- meal_number_candidates()/rewrite_search_query() (menu_utils.py) stay mode-agnostic catalog primitives, so this smoke expectation keeps proving both breakfast and lunch candidates for number "1" resolve regardless of any session's bound mode.
greetingSubstring: Welcome to McDonald's! What can I get started for you today?
